judgment.notes: M002 is applied with A=ℂ, T=V and the common basis from H006: finite-dimensionality comes from H004, finite basis indexing and the strong rank premise are positively checked in BG001–BG002. Its cardinal count is n by H004/D001, matching N001; BG003 checks the reindexing. M001 uses A=ℤ, B=R, T=M, Q=I and the F001 basis; S001 establishes the fraction subring, and M is an abelian group with its integer module structure. Its conclusion supplies exactly the tensor basis used in S002. M006 uses ℓ=p and arbitrary natural t from 0≤t≤λ; H001 and H003 establish both premises. BG005 checks its nondivisibility bridge. No E applications occur.

S001 correctly obtains a common I-indexed basis and verifies R's ring closure (BG001–BG004). In S002 every tensor has a finite expansion in the M001 basis; its image is ∑r_i f_i, so complex independence and R⊂ℂ force its coefficients to vanish. This proves injectivity without a flatness/localization theorem, and the image contains the complex basis and is its R-span. S003 uses U_Z-stability for each divided power, linearity for the R-span, and h=xy−yx for stability and the induced bracket action. For each t≤λ<p, the factorial theorem plus BG005 gives a valid inverse in R; BG006 verifies the binomial inverse. S004 correctly computes the images: X_λ is zero below λ and sends e_λ to e_0; Y_λ returns e_0 to e_λ; X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i. In the last projection product the k<j, k=j and k>j cases are exhaustive and give precisely binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. Composing yields the stated E_ij formula; R-linearity and the scalar inverse prove preservation. BG007 justifies testing equality on the basis. All formulas remain valid at λ=0 and at i,j=0,λ; no distinctness of weights modulo p is used.

Every direct input has an actual role: H001 gives prime denominator closure and the factorial premise; H003 bounds factorial indices; H004 supplies dimension and Chevalley brackets; H006 supplies the common lattice basis and divided-power stability; N001 supplies card(I), the e-basis and the full divided-power formulas; M001 supplies the tensor basis; M002 performs the complex basis count; M006 supplies factorial coprimality. Seven recorded notes transparently account for routine finite-basis/rank/cardinality, prime-divisibility, binomial and basis-coordinate steps. The core tensor injectivity argument and the matrix-unit construction are actually displayed, not hidden in a localization or structure theorem. No extra H, project lemma or E is imported.

The prose uses only the supplied H/M/N statements, expanded definitions, earlier in-scope facts and the seven positively checked background notes. F001 is established before choosing f, F002 establishes the embedding before image identification and preservation, and F003 establishes the scalar units and stability before S004. S004 instantiates the formulas actually exported by N001, without borrowing its producer's proof or additional highest-weight facts. Equalities of operators follow from their displayed basis images. No ancestor statement, reduction theorem, flatness theorem or hidden modular-weight argument is needed.
